item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03060","case1_error":"No clear error: correctly reports 4 movies and 16 books; the question permits separate counts.","case2_error":"Invents a repeating initial schedule, evaluates 10+3+10+1 as 14, and incorrectly computes remaining time and stops.","reason":"Case 1 correctly answers a reasonable reading of the question, so both cases do not have clear mathematical errors.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J03061","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written calorie sum as 2175 instead of 1975.","case2_error":"Moves the second five-chip serving to day two and delays the daily ten-chip schedule to day three.","reason":"Case 1 is numerical evaluation error; case 2 changes the stated timeline while performing its arithmetic correctly.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03062","case1_error":"Leading answer marker says 20, but the derivation correctly calculates and rounds to 15 minutes.","case2_error":"Treats Robert as Bob, increasing Bob's cats despite the question naming Robert as recipient.","reason":"Case 1 has only an answer-marker conflict, which requires an uncertain judgment regardless of case 2.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J03063","case1_error":"Omits the stated 20% primer discount, using full-price primer in the total.","case2_error":"Incorrectly defines total spending as skates cost plus remaining cash, rather than starting cash minus remaining cash.","reason":"Ignoring a price discount differs from using an erroneous cash-balance relation to determine spending.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03064","case1_error":"Uses one bottle's 80-load capacity as the total capacity for two bottles.","case2_error":"Sets feeding cost equal to purchase cost, omitting the stated 20% increase.","reason":"Case 1 fails to scale capacity by bottle count; case 2 fails to apply a percentage increase to feeding cost.","judgment":"different"}]}
